audit_status.review_note: Divine hiddenness, predatory power, poor and vulnerable people, violence, and justice.

notes.title: Psalm 9–10 acrostic relationship
notes.body: Psalm 10 continues patterns begun in Psalm 9 and is joined to it in some ancient traditions. The project preserves received Hebrew/KJV chapter numbering while flagging the literary relationship.

verses.restored: The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.

familiar.text: The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.

familiar.text: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see it.

translation_notes: This chapter expands corpus coverage while remaining explicitly pending a deeper Hebrew/source-witness audit. KJV is retained only as the familiar comparison layer.

The completion draft intentionally preserves coherent traditional English syntax where a verse has not yet received a curated Hebrew-sensitive rendering; it does not mix archaic and modern grammar. Major identified lexical/textual issues receive explicit overrides and notes.
safety_note: The psalm describes predatory abuse of the poor; it should strengthen protection of vulnerable people, not stigmatize poverty.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Scrolls where extant, and other relevant witnesses during the global audit.
Audit Psalms 9–10 together for alphabetic-acrostic structure and numbering differences across traditions.
